title: Additions Represented by Print Symbols

illustrates.quote: Represent a dash, hyphen, or special print sign (often unspaced) used to indicate the omission of a word or word part to which an addition is to be made by the braille hyphen.

print.printFeatures: A simple list of unnumbered entry items.

braille.notes: Left margin is 9 cells (stripped). The braille lines correspond exactly to the 5 printed items.

uncertain: The special print sign in 'là-∞' looks like an infinity symbol, though slightly clipped. Recorded as ∞.
The print symbol in 'der Spass, -̈e' is a hyphen with a diaeresis above it, transcribed as -̈ based on the braille modifier ⠸⠒ (diaeresis).
The print symbol in 'il -̂t' is a hyphen with a circumflex above it, transcribed as -̂ based on the braille modifier ⠸⠩ (circumflex).
